q: When ionic compounds dissolve in water, ______ reactions occur. (2024)
e: When ionic compounds dissolve in water, they dissociate into hydrated ions.

q: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that ______ ionise only to a limited extent in water. (2025)
e: Weak acids undergo partial ionization in aqueous solutions.

q: Which of the following is the strongest conjugate base? (2026)
e: CH3COO- is the conjugate base of a weak acid (ethanoic acid), making it the strongest conjugate base among the choices.

q: ______ base is sodium hydroxide. (2024)
e: Sodium hydroxide dissociates in water to yield hydroxide ions, fitting the Arrhenius definition of a base.

q: CH3COO- is the ______ of ethanoic acid. (2024)
e: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, so its conjugate base (CH3COO-) is relatively strong.

q: What is the pH of a sample of black coffee that has a hydrogen ion concentration of 7.8 × 10^-6 mol dm^-3? (2026)
Which element is always present in Arrhenius acid? (2025)
e: Arrhenius acids produce H+ ions in aqueous solution, so hydrogen is always present.

q: Which of the following salts dissolves in water to give a solution with a pH greater than 7? (2025)
e: Sodium ethanoate is formed from a weak acid and strong base, hydrolyzing to produce a basic solution (pH > 7).

q: The combination that would buffer the pH at about 4.7 is ______. (2024)
e: HCOOH and HCOONa form an acidic buffer system effective around pH 4.7.

q: In pure water, one H2O molecule donates a proton and acts as an/a ______. (2026)
e: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, a proton donor acts as an acid.

q: ______ represents an acid-base reaction. (2026)
e: The reaction between HBr (acid) and KOH (base) produces salt and water, representing a neutralization reaction.

q: When NH4NO3 dissolves in water, the pH becomes less than 7 because the hydrolysis of ______. (2025)
e: NH4+ reacts with water to release H+ ions, making the solution acidic.

q: What is the pH of black coffee with a hydrogen ion concentration of 7.8 × 10^-6 mol dm^-3? (2025)
Choose the strong acid from the following. (2024)
e: H2SO4 is a strong mineral acid that fully dissociates in water.

q: When HCOOK dissolves in water, the pH becomes greater than 7 because the hydrolysis of ______. (2024)
e: HCOO- hydrolyzes in water to produce OH- ions, resulting in a basic solution.

q: Which one of the following solutions is not a buffer solution? (2025)
e: HBr is a strong acid, so HBr/KBr cannot function as a buffer solution.

q: A buffer solution of pH ______ can be prepared with a weak base and its salt. (2025)
e: A basic buffer consisting of a weak base and its conjugate salt maintains pH in the range of 7–11.

q: The basicity of sulphuric acid is ______. (2025)
e: Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) contains two replaceable hydrogen ions per molecule.

q: A buffer solution of pH ______ can be prepared with a weak base and its salt. (2025)
e: Weak base buffers operate within a basic pH range of 7–11.

q: Which of the following is the strongest conjugate base? (2026)
e: CH3COO- is derived from a weak acid, so it acts as a stronger conjugate base than those derived from strong acids.

q: The definition of Bronsted-Lowry acid applies to all solvents, not only to ______ solutions. (2026)
e: The Brønsted-Lowry concept generalizes acid-base behavior beyond aqueous solutions.

q: A solutions with pOH of 11.0 would be described as a (an) ______ solution. (2026)
e: pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 11.0 = 3.0, which indicates an acidic solution.
